Where it began

François du Plessis, known to everyone as Faf, was born in Pretoria on 13 July 1984. Sport ran in the family: his father, who shares his first name, played rugby in the centres for Northern Transvaal in the 1980s. At Affies, the Afrikaans boys' high school in Pretoria, his schoolmates included Jacques Rudolph, Heino Kuhn and a certain AB de Villiers, and he went on to the University of Pretoria.

He learned a good deal of his cricket in England, first in league cricket in Nottinghamshire and Lancashire, then with Lancashire from 2008, where his fielding won warm praise from the coach, Mike Watkinson.

The player

His Test debut came at Adelaide in November 2012, when he was brought in at number six. With South Africa trying to hold on for a draw, he batted 466 minutes for 110 not out and saved the match. He was only the fourth South African to make a hundred on Test debut, and in 2020 cricket.com.au judged it the best Test innings played in Australia since 2000. A year later he made 134 against India as South Africa chased 458 and finished eight runs short of a famous win.

He played 69 Tests between 2012 and 2021, scoring 4,163 runs at 40.03 with 10 hundreds and 21 fifties, and held 63 catches. His best was 199 against Sri Lanka at Centurion in December 2020. He led South Africa in 36 Tests, winning 18, and was the first captain from any country to beat Australia in Australia in all three formats.

What made him special

Patience and nerve. When a Test needed saving, du Plessis was the man most likely to dig in for hour after hour. He was a brilliant fielder as well, and his captaincy rested on team spirit and on hearing out his players. He also played 108 international innings before he made his first duck, a record.

One-day hundreds were slower to arrive; his first came in his 51st match. Then, in 2014, he made three in a row and was on 96 in the next, needing one run to win, when AB de Villiers hit two sixes and a four in quick succession. Du Plessis had to go for a boundary and was caught. Old school friends can be like that.

Away from the middle

He became the first South African to make hundreds in all three international formats, and in 2019 Cricket South Africa named him its men's cricketer of the year. After leaving Tests in 2021 he carried on in franchise cricket around the world, captaining sides in the IPL, the SA20 and Major League Cricket, and leading Saint Lucia Kings to the Caribbean Premier League title in 2024.

His autobiography, FAF: Through Fire, came out in October 2022.

And finally

His old school friend de Villiers once recorded a song, and du Plessis turned up in the music video. A man who could bat for 466 minutes in Adelaide was clearly happy to do a favour for a friend.
